Chapter 1 · November 2025

It started with being found

Deka's Zoca story did not start with AI on the phones. It started with two studios, Wexford and Greentree, that wanted more of their neighborhood to find them on Google. They turned on Discovery, Zoca's organic growth engine. Zero ad spend. It runs continuously:

Google Business Profile optimization

The studio's Google listing kept complete, accurate, and tuned for what nearby searchers type.

Blogs, written and published

Fresh, locally relevant content on the studio's website, on autopilot.

Google Posts

Regular updates and offers published straight to the Google listing.

Constant keyword optimization

Website and profile continuously re-tuned as search behavior shifts.

Demand and competition analytics

What people nearby search for, and where competitors rank, feeding every optimization above.

Chapter 2 · July 2026

The phones: answered in one ring, around the clock

So Deka came to Zoca with the ask that started it all: put AI on the phones. In July 2026 the AI receptionist went live across all four studios.

Picks up instantly, 24/7

Evenings, Sundays, holidays, mid-appointment rushes. No ring-outs, no voicemail.

Books on the call

Checks the live calendar and confirms the appointment in seconds, while the caller is still on the line.

Reschedules and cancels

Handles changes end to end on the call itself. No hold, no callback, no front-desk interruption.

Filters spam

Robocalls and solicitors are caught and dropped before the phone ever reaches a human.

Knows the studio

Services, prices, policies, intro offers. Answers the routine questions that used to eat front-desk time.

Hands off and learns

Anything it cannot answer goes straight to Deka's customer support team. Every question they answer gets added to its knowledge, so it handles more on its own every week.

Same conversion as a human. A far better experience.

Deka's baseline with humans on the phones was about 20% of incoming calls converting to a booking. The AI receptionist holds that same rate, while answering every call instantly, around the clock, with spam already filtered out. Before, a call during an appointment or after hours was simply a missed call. Now every call gets handled.

The control room

Every conversation, every call, in one dashboard

  • Every call recorded, transcribed, and summarized. Play any call back, read what happened in one glance.
  • Texts and calls in one inbox, with status tags like Checkout Link Sent and Needs Action, so nothing falls through.
  • Jump in any time. Staff can take over any conversation by text or call from the same screen.
  • Rate the AI on every interaction. Thumbs up or down feeds straight back into how it behaves.
  • Analytics across the whole system: bookings, calls, follow-ups, campaigns.
Chapter 3 · The part nobody asked for

Same weeks, one month apart: 54 bookings became 149.

The AI receptionist did not ship alone. It came with something Deka had no idea they needed: a rebuilt Booking Widget and automatic recovery of abandoned bookings. It turned into the biggest win of the whole rollout. July 17 to August 15, right after launch, the Greentree, Wexford and Washington studios took 149 website bookings. The same weeks one month earlier: 54. Same studios, same websites, same kind of visitor. Here is exactly why.

Side by side, step by step

The Booking Widget vs the old Mindbody flow

Both flows below were walked on the same day, on the same studio's website, on a phone. Left is Zoca's Booking Widget. Right is the legacy Mindbody flow it runs beside.

Zoca Booking Widget
Mindbody
Step 1

Who is booking? Zoca asks first. Mindbody asks last.

  • Name and phone upfront. Email optional. Returning visitors are autofilled.
  • Every visitor becomes a known lead before they see a single service.
  • Drop off at any later step and Zoca knows exactly who to follow up with.
  • Identity is asked at the very end: first a Mindbody account, then a long profile form.
  • Required fields include phone, birthdate, and a full street address.
  • Drop off before this point and the studio never knows you existed. Industry wide, roughly 2 of 3 mobile checkouts are abandoned.
Step 2

Finding a service

  • Services pre-expanded with real prices, searchable, one tap between categories.
  • Intro offers built in: $139.99 for new guests with the $210 regular price struck through. The deal sells itself.
  • A bare list of collapsed categories. No prices.
  • Expand a category: still no prices, just "Show Details" and "Select".
  • A price finally appears only after committing to a service.
Step 3

Add-ons

  • Add a service and extras appear right beneath it, exact prices, same page.
  • Upsell happens at the moment of highest intent, with zero extra navigation.
  • Add-ons live on a separate page, one more screen between the guest and the calendar.
  • Prices are vague "Starting at" ranges.
Step 4

Booking two services in one visit

  • Lashes plus brows in one appointment, one cart, with a running service count.
  • Bigger tickets without a second booking flow.
✕
Not possible

Mindbody books one service at a time. Want brows too? Start the whole flow again.

Step 5

Picking your artist

  • Skill tags with exact pricing: "Master Lash Artist Upgrade | $20". No surprises at checkout.
  • Cart summary pinned on top, Continue button always visible.
  • Upgrade pricing shown as a vague "$10-$20" range.
  • No sticky button. Guests must scroll past every provider to find Continue.
Step 6

Date and time

  • Clean slot grid with the full appointment summary pinned below: services, artist, duration, total.
  • Sticky Continue keeps the guest moving.
  • Lands on a "fully booked" dead end for today, with a grayed-out button.
  • The guest has to hunt forward for availability day by day.
Step 7

Checkout

  • Card on file, no charge today. Secures the slot without scaring the guest.
  • Slot reserved with a live countdown, promo code field, cancellation policy acknowledged inline.
  • One screen. Done.
  • "Add to Cart" leads to the account wall and profile form from Step 1.
  • The hardest part of the flow is saved for the moment the guest is most likely to quit.

And when they drop off anyway: Zoca goes and gets them

This is the part Deka had no idea existed. Because contact info is captured in Step 1, every abandoned booking triggers an automatic follow-up by text and AI call to finish the job.

34 recovered bookings in 10 weeks $4,470 in recovered value Nearly 1 in 10 website bookings is now a recovered booking This channel produced exactly zero before

Chapter 5 · And then they come back

Loyalty: campaigns that fire on real client behavior

With the front door handled, the next question was the back door: clients who visit once and drift away. Not a blast list. Campaigns are built on triggers from what actually happens in the studio, and run themselves by text:

Trigger: service booked

Kick off pre-visit touchpoints the moment an appointment lands on the calendar.

Trigger: service attended

Follow up after the visit: rebook nudges, refill reminders timed to the service, review asks.

Trigger: client going quiet

Win-back campaigns start automatically when a client's next visit is overdue.

In lashes, the client who returns for a second visit is the one who stays for years. More than 200 Deka clients are already in active campaigns.

Chapter 6 · The newest layer

Paid ads with instant follow-up

The latest addition to the stack: Zoca-run ad campaigns where every lead gets automated follow-up the moment it lands. Of the current cycle of roughly 24 leads, 4 have already booked, 1 is mid-booking, and about 63% are still being actively worked. Nothing sits cold in an inbox.
